issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies addGuestStudents(int) as returning void, but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) returning boolean. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected method signature and return behavior (whether they should return a success flag or not). The template leaves a TODO for this method without a signature, so the authoritative UML in the problem statement indicates void; the solution diverges by returning a boolean.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's addGuestStudents(int) to return void (perform the update without returning a value) to match the UML and problem statement, or (B) update the problem statement/UML to indicate boolean as the return type and clarify the meaning (e.g., returns true on success, false on invalid input). Also update the template TODO/signature to match the chosen return type so students implement the correct signature.
